readings_chosen: Sentence 1: ‘told a story in which’ explicitly introduces a told world, not a supposition layered on actual facts. I record the telling in the actual ledger and the open door only in nora_story. ‘Stood open’ is a state description, not the body-response class heavy and standing and not a shaped physical happening.

Sentence 2: ‘she told it’ refers back to Nora’s already recorded telling. The room supplies actual spatial context; the door’s shut state is CLAIMED there. I retain ‘stayed shut’ as a Fact and encode its express exclusion of open as denied(open(door)), both guarded by the same source line actualshut. This is lexical negation of open, not an added premise or a rule producing shutness.

Sentences 1–2: the definite ‘the door’ permits one door described differently across the two worlds, or separate counterparts. I use one name with disjoint standing, without asserting a cross-world identity fact. Each world receives its own thing line so the told world inherits nothing. No state changes within either world, so no sequence of opening and closing is invented.

Sentence 1: tell stays tell, without a replacement shape. Nora is only a thing and doer; the story is not assigned the response class ‘not a body’ merely from background knowledge. No body response or direction is supplied. The did and holds clauses for telling represent the same source happening.
